## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limpa, dplyr, stringr, purrr, readr, writexl)
here::i_am("01_Preprocess/01_Filtering/a_script/01_filter.qmd")
```

## Read measurements

`readDIANN()` reads DIA-NN's normalised intensity (`Precursor.Normalised`) for each precursor, a
peptide at one charge state, and keeps those passing its default 0.01 cutoffs on `Q.Value`,
`Lib.Q.Value` and `Lib.PG.Q.Value`. The limpa vignette gives these cutoffs for a match-between-runs
(MBR) search, where an identification in one run supports the same peptide in others; whether this
search used MBR is unrecorded. Protein-level normalisation comes after quantification, in
`02_Quantification`.

`y$E` holds log2 intensities, precursors in rows and runs in columns; `y$genes` holds their
annotations. `Protein.Ids` is added to the default annotation columns because the repair below
needs it. `NA` marks a missing measurement.

```{r read}
y <- readDIANN(
  here("00_Input", "report.parquet"),
  annotation.columns = c(
    "Protein.Group", "Protein.Ids", "Protein.Names",
    "Genes", "Proteotypic"
  )
)
dim(y)
head(y$genes, 6)
y$E[1:6, 1:4]
```

## Match samples

Run names are matched to the metadata ignoring letter case (one run, `Cl_MDR_7E-T2`, is written
`CL_MDR_7E-T2` in the sheet), and the columns are reordered and renamed to sample IDs. Every
metadata run must be in the report; the report's runs left out are printed. One is the discarded
S08 injection, in the report but not the metadata.

```{r map-samples}
metadata <- read_csv(here("00_Input", "metadata.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
i <- match(str_to_lower(metadata$run), str_to_lower(colnames(y)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
setdiff(colnames(y), colnames(y)[i])
y <- y[, i]
colnames(y) <- metadata$sample_id
# EList subsetting expects targets to be a data.frame, not a tibble.
y$targets <- data.frame(metadata, row.names = metadata$sample_id)
head(y$targets[c("run", "sample_id", "participant", "leg", "treatment", "timepoint")], 6)
```

Signal, the summed intensity on the natural scale, shows how much a filter removes, which
precursor counts alone cannot. `total_signal()` computes it from log2 values; the starting signal
stays fixed, so the percentages from different filters compare.

```{r starting-signal}
total_signal <- function(log2_intensities) {
  sum(2^log2_intensities, na.rm = TRUE)
}

signal_start <- total_signal(y$E)
```

## Repair annotations

The search FASTA appended the cRAP database of common laboratory contaminants, which lists some
human proteins the human FASTA already holds. DIA-NN therefore reports myoglobin as
`P02144;cRAP-P02144` and marks it non-proteotypic (not unique to one protein), along with creatine
kinase M and both haemoglobins. Left unrepaired, the shared-peptide filter below deletes them.

Two kinds of row are dropped: protein groups made only of cRAP entries, and reversed sequences
(`rev_`), which the FASTA carried as ordinary entries, so DIA-NN treated them as real. Mixed groups
stay for repair.

```{r identify-annotation-artefacts}
members <- str_split(y$genes$Protein.Group, ";")
crap_only <- map_lgl(members, function(ids) all(str_starts(ids, "cRAP-")))
is_decoy <- str_starts(y$genes$Protein.Group, "rev_")
mentions_crap <- str_detect(y$genes$Protein.Ids, "cRAP-")
removed_rows <- crap_only | is_decoy
```

Counts and signal per category, before the rows go. The categories overlap, and "mentions cRAP
at all" is counted, not removed.

```{r annotation-counts}
reasons <- list(
  "cRAP-only group" = crap_only,
  "reversed decoy" = is_decoy,
  "mentions cRAP at all" = mentions_crap
)
removal_counts <- tibble(
  reason = names(reasons),
  precursors = map_int(reasons, sum),
  pct_signal = 100 * map_dbl(reasons, function(rows) {
    total_signal(y$E[rows, , drop = FALSE])
  }) / signal_start
)
```

```{r annotation-preview}
tibble(
  category = c("cRAP-only", "mixed cRAP", "reversed decoy"),
  precursors = c(sum(crap_only), sum(mentions_crap & !crap_only), sum(is_decoy))
)
show_cols <- c("Protein.Group", "Protein.Ids", "Genes", "Proteotypic")
head(y$genes[which(crap_only), show_cols], 6)
head(y$genes[which(is_decoy), show_cols], 6)
```

Remove flagged rows first, so every row left to repair keeps at least one human entry. The preview
shows retained cRAP rows before repair.

```{r remove-annotation-artefacts}
y <- y[!removed_rows, ]
repair_examples <- head(which(mentions_crap[!removed_rows]), 6)
y$genes[repair_examples, show_cols]
```

Drop every cRAP entry, not just its prefix, then recompute `Proteotypic`, the flag the next filter
uses to find uniquely assigned evidence. cRAP holds other species' copies (`cRAP-P00883;P04075` is
rabbit and human ALDOA), and a stripped prefix would leave those proteins looking shared.

```{r repair-annotations}
y$genes <- y$genes |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Protein.Group, Protein.Ids, Protein.Names, Genes),
      function(x) {
        str_split(x, ";") |> map(str_subset, "^cRAP-", negate = TRUE) |> map_chr(str_flatten, ";")
      }
    ),
    # mutate() evaluates in order, so this reads the repaired Protein.Ids above.
    Proteotypic = if_else(
      mentions_crap[!removed_rows],
      as.integer(!str_detect(Protein.Ids, ";")),
      as.integer(Proteotypic)
    )
  )
```

The same rows after repair:

```{r repaired-annotation-preview}
y$genes[repair_examples, show_cols]
```

## Remove ambiguous assignments

`filterNonProteotypicPeptides()` removes precursors shared between protein groups, and
`filterCompoundProteins()` removes compound groups, those naming more than one protein, in the
limpa vignette's order. The vignette calls `filterSingletonPeptides()` optional and recommends
keeping all proteins, so it is not applied. Nothing is filtered on missing values: `dpc()` models
how the chance of detection rises with intensity, so a missing value carries information.

`step_summary()` returns one row per filter.

```{r limpa-filters}
step_summary <- function(elist, step, starting_signal) {
  tibble(
    step = step,
    precursors = nrow(elist),
    protein_groups = n_distinct(elist$genes$Protein.Group),
    pct_signal = 100 * total_signal(elist$E) / starting_signal
  )
}

filter_log <- step_summary(y, "repaired", signal_start)
y <- filterNonProteotypicPeptides(y)
filter_log <- bind_rows(filter_log, step_summary(y, "shared peptides removed", signal_start))
y <- filterCompoundProteins(y)
filter_log <- bind_rows(filter_log, step_summary(y, "compound groups removed", signal_start))
```

## Filter contaminants

A needle biopsy carries blood and passes through skin. These proteins are removed here, before
quantification, because `dpc()` fits one detection curve across every precursor and `dpcQuant()`
takes its prior from all the data. That order is a project choice: limpa's ccRCC case study removes
immunoglobulins after `dpcQuant()` instead.

The 4 family patterns match immunoglobulin, keratin, SPRR (small proline-rich proteins of skin)
and haemoglobin names; `^` and `$`
require a whole-name match, so `KRTCAP2` is not caught. The 147 individual symbols are plasma,
red-cell, platelet, neutrophil and skin proteins, picked by judgement from the dataset's gene
symbols on 2026-09-04 with Human Protein Atlas (HPA) single-cell expression in view. No script
produced the list.

A scripted rule was tried in its place on 2026-10-13: remove a gene when HPA finds it specific to
blood, immune, skin or liver cells and does not detect it in myonuclei. It kept 86 proteins this
list removes, many of them complement and other plasma proteins that the muscle's own fibroblasts
and vessels also make (C3, C1R, C1S and SERPING1 all have muscle RNA in HPA). With those proteins
in, the baseline BFR against HLRT comparison, where counterbalanced legs should differ by nothing,
flagged 21 gene sets in stage 03's fgsea, all complement, coagulation, immunoglobulin or red-cell,
against 1 with this list. No annotation rule tried could tell plasma-borne complement from locally
made complement, so the list stays. It predates that comparison, which therefore checks the list
rather than tuning it.

```{r contaminant-rules}
contaminant_families <- str_c("^(", str_flatten(c(
  "IG[HKL][VDJCAGMEL]([0-9][0-9A-Z-]*)?", "KRT([0-9]|AP)[0-9A-Z-]*",
  "SPRR[0-9][0-9A-Z]*", "HB[ABDGMQZ][0-9]?"
), "|"), ")$")

contaminant_symbols <- c(
  "JCHAIN", "HRNR", "DCD", "SBSN", "CSTA", "AHSP",
  "A1BG", "AFM", "AGT", "AHSG", "ALB", "AMBP", "APCS", "APOA1", "APOA2", "APOA4", "APOB",
  "APOC1", "APOC2", "APOC3", "APOD", "APOE", "APOF", "APOH", "APOL1", "APOL2", "APOM",
  "ARHGDIB", "AZGP1", "BCAM", "BTD", "C1QB", "C1QC", "C1R", "C1RL", "C1S", "C2", "C3",
  "C4A", "C4B", "C4BPA", "C4BPB", "C5", "C6", "C7", "C8A", "C8B", "C8G", "C9", "CA1",
  "CFB", "CFD", "CFH", "CFHR2", "CFHR5", "CFI", "CLEC3B", "CLU", "CP", "CPB2", "CPN1",
  "CPN2", "CTSG", "DEFA1", "DMTN", "ELANE", "EPB42", "F10", "F11", "F12", "F13A1", "F13B",
  "F2", "F9", "FCN3", "FERMT3", "FETUB", "FGA", "FGB", "FGG", "FYB1", "GC", "GIMAP1",
  "GIMAP4", "GMFG", "GP1BA", "GPLD1", "GYPC", "HABP2", "HP", "HPR", "HPX", "HRG",
  "IGFALS", "ITIH1", "ITIH3", "KEL", "KLKB1", "KNG1", "LBP", "LCAT", "LCP1", "LPA",
  "LRG1", "LTF", "LYZ", "MASP1", "MPO", "MPP1", "NCF1", "ORM1", "ORM2", "PF4", "PGLYRP2",
  "PLG", "PLTP", "PON1", "PPBP", "PROS1", "PRTN3", "PZP", "RBP4", "RHCE", "RNASE3",
  "S100A8", "S100A9", "SAA1", "SAA4", "SELENOP", "SERPINA1", "SERPINA3", "SERPINA4",
  "SERPINA5", "SERPINA6", "SERPINA7", "SERPINC1", "SERPIND1", "SERPINF2", "SERPING1",
  "SHBG", "SLC4A1", "SPTA1", "TF", "TTR", "TUBB1", "VTN", "VWF"
)
```

A group is removed only when every gene symbol on it matches a listed symbol or a family pattern,
so a contaminant sharing a group with a muscle protein stays. `by_symbol` records whether the
listed symbols alone cover the group; it only labels the summary.

```{r flag-contaminants}
gene_symbols <- str_split(str_to_upper(y$genes$Genes), ";")

by_symbol <- map_lgl(gene_symbols, function(symbols) all(symbols %in% contaminant_symbols))
contaminant <- map_lgl(gene_symbols, function(symbols) {
  all(symbols %in% contaminant_symbols | str_detect(symbols, contaminant_families))
})
head(y$genes[which(contaminant), c("Protein.Group", "Genes")], 6)
```

Signal removed per gene-symbol string and matching route, as a percentage of starting signal;
"family" means the listed symbols alone did not cover the group.

```{r measure-excluded-signal}
contaminants_removed <- tibble(
  symbol = y$genes$Genes[contaminant],
  matched_by = if_else(by_symbol[contaminant], "symbol", "family"),
  signal = rowSums(2^y$E[contaminant, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
) |>
  summarise(
    precursors = n(), pct_signal = 100 * sum(signal) / signal_start,
    .by = c(symbol, matched_by)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_signal))
```

The fraction removed from each sample uses that sample's signal just before this filter as its
denominator, so uneven contamination between samples and groups is visible.

```{r measure-sample-fractions}
contaminant_fraction <- colSums(2^y$E[contaminant, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
  colSums(2^y$E, na.rm = TRUE)
sample_contamination <- tibble(
  sample_id = colnames(y),
  group = y$targets$group,
  pct_signal_removed = 100 * contaminant_fraction
)
```

```{r remove-contaminants}
y <- y[!contaminant, ]
filter_log <- bind_rows(filter_log, step_summary(y, "contaminants removed", signal_start))
```

## Filtering summary

Rows, distinct protein groups and percentage of starting signal after each filter, then the
annotation exclusions. Signal percentages describe measured intensity, not protein mass.

```{r filtering-summary}
filter_log
removal_counts
```

The 20 removed gene-symbol strings carrying the most signal.

```{r removed-contaminants}
head(contaminants_removed, 20)
```

The median removed fraction per treatment and timepoint group, then the five most contaminated
samples, which a median hides. Nothing tests or adjusts for either.

```{r contaminant-fractions}
round(tapply(contaminant_fraction, y$targets$group, median), 4)
slice_max(sample_contamination, pct_signal_removed, n = 5)
```

## Save results

`precursors_filtered.rds` holds the filtered measurements for protein quantification, and
`01_filter.xlsx` the summaries, both in `c_data/`. Rerun protein quantification whenever this
matrix changes.

```{r write}
out <- here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data")
saveRDS(y, file.path(out, "precursors_filtered.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  list(
    samples = as.data.frame(y$targets),
    filtering_summary = filter_log,
    annotation_exclusions = removal_counts,
    removed_contaminants = contaminants_removed,
    sample_contamination = sample_contamination
  ),
  file.path(out, "01_filter.xlsx")
)
```
